rows.subtopic: Domains, Ranges and Principal Value Branches
rows.figure: REQUIRED — the stem names no curve at all, so the question IS the printed graph. It shows several branches of the inverse-cotangent relation with horizontal dashed asymptotes at \(y = -\pi\), \(y = \pi\) and \(y = 2\pi\), the axis marked at \(\pm\pi/2\) and \(3\pi/2\), and the principal branch falling from near \(\pi\) through \((0,\ \pi/2)\) towards \(0\). Page idx 4.

rows.stem: Let \(f(x) = x^2\), \(x \in R\). Then, which of the following statements is **incorrect** ?

options.label: A
options.text: Minimum value of f does not exist.

options.label: B
options.text: There is no point of maximum value of f in R.

rows.subtopic: Order and Degree of a Differential Equation
rows.stem:
The order and degree of the differential equation

\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 4\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = x \log\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)\)

are respectively :
Chances that three persons A, B, and C go to the market are 30%, 60% and 50% respectively. The probability that at least one will go to the market is :
Determine those values of x for which \(f(x) = \dfrac{2}{x} - 5\), \(x \ne 0\) is increasing or decreasing.

Find the value of \(\lambda\) if the following lines are perpendicular to each other :

\(l_1 : \dfrac{1 - x}{-3} = \dfrac{3y - 2}{2\lambda} = \dfrac{z - 3}{3}\)

\(l_2 : \dfrac{x - 1}{3\lambda} = \dfrac{1 - y}{1} = \dfrac{2z - 5}{3}\)

If \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}\), are three matrices, then find ABC.

A coin is biased so that the head is 3 times as likely to occur as tail. If the coin is tossed three times, find the probability distribution of number of tails. Hence, find the mean of the distribution.
Use integration to find the area of the region enclosed by curve \(y = -x^2\) and the straight lines \(x = -3\), \(x = 2\) and \(y = 0\). Sketch a rough figure to illustrate the bounded region.

rows.subtopic: Equation of a Line in Space
rows.stem: Find the foot of the perpendicular drawn from point \((2, -1, 5)\) to the line \(\dfrac{x - 11}{10} = \dfrac{y + 2}{-4} = \dfrac{z + 8}{-11}\). Also, find the length of the perpendicular.
